lines.narration: The deadliest hunter on Earth is a virus shaped like a moon lander.
It's called a bacteriophage, and it only hunts bacteria.
It lands on one, legs first, and grips the surface.
Then it squats, and punches a needle through the wall.
Its DNA shoots inside, and takes over the cell.
The bacterium stops living, and starts building phages.
In half an hour, it is packed with a hundred copies.
Then they dissolve the wall from inside. Pop.
Every one flies off to find another.
In the oceans, viruses kill a fifth of all microbes, every day.
And they can't touch you. Human cells are not on the menu.
The deadliest hunter on Earth is not hunting you.
